Played on Madhouse as my first time, 7h20 playthrough. Probably the worst mainline RE game at the time it was released due to subpar action sequences, bosses & enemy variety & a story that could have used a lot more setup. The setting kinda just amounts to what if we made RE outlast, but there wasn't any horror besides some restricted gore elements. Sometimes your character kinda just decides to move like he's stuck in sinking sand. Sucks that I had to pay to unlock the hardest difficulty from the get go too & the boat section is the worst out of RE, it's both horrible and overstays its welcome.
 A "strong" 5/10

I started playing Resident Evil 7 yesterday and finished it in the same day. i played it for 8 hours straight.

I kept postponing the game because I thought I would hate the first person perspective, but surprisingly, I loved it. Resident Evil 7 was a great experience after the disappointment of Resident Evil 6.

Fighting the Baker family members was awesome and almost everything in the game was enjoyable. i never got bored. the only part where I felt a little bored was the ship section.

the game wasn't as scary as people described it. In my opinion people were exaggerating.

i would Absolutely recommend playing it.
But the real question is... Who the hell is Aunt Rhody and what do i tell her ?

Resident Evil 7 = 8.5/10

Man, I have a special affection for this game, but in this review I’ll try to stay neutral. I spent basically the entire Xbox 360 and PS3 generation without gaming. I was a teenager, wanted to go out more, and ended up spending years away from video games. But when I saw the trailer for Resident Evil 7, I completely lost my mind. Back then, Mia looked insanely realistic — her hair, facial features — and the similarities to Outlast immediately caught my attention.

I genuinely became obsessed with the game and wanted to play RE7 no matter what, so I ended up buying a PS4. (At the time I already had a PC, but I still preferred playing on consoles.)

The experience was incredible. I absolutely loved this game. I thought the gameplay was amazing, and honestly, I never found it as terrifying as many people claimed. To me, this game feels a lot like those 1980s horror movies filled with cheesy gore and cheap practical effects.

Man, fighting Jack is almost hilarious at times, especially during the garage fight and when he grabs that giant pair of pruning shears.

Negative points:

- This game honestly could have had a different title and worked as a parallel story within the Resident Evil universe. Even though I really love this game, I still don’t truly feel like I’m playing Resident Evil. And honestly, making it a numbered Resident Evil game makes it even weirder hahaha.

- The ship section with Mia is extremely boring and should have been skippable. In RE9 I hate playing as Chloe, and in RE2 Remake I hate playing as Sherry, but at least those sections are short. With Mia on the ship, it feels like it never ends. It’s extremely irritating.

- There’s no option to skip cutscenes, and that makes replaying the game much more annoying.

citations.review_text: Very nice, very cool, runs smooth, very few bugs

This resident evil was a breath of fresh air after playing the more action oriented entries in the series. I almost kind of missed the more survival horror aspect of the RE2 remake so to see that come back in this entry in a big way was a great (and horrifying) feeling. I almost want to say that this is better overall than the Resident Evil 2 remake because the feeling of “nope, don’t wanna go there” started right at the very beginning. Seeing the old run down house invoked a level of uneasiness that I rarely get in a game. The last game to make me feel like that was Dead Space. Let’s get into all the pieces that make this game great and some nitpicks that almost ruin my immersion.

First off, the graphic, environmental art, and the characters contribute greatly to the the horror aspect of this. The first person view of seeing this game without a character in the way really made me take in all the creepy, gross, or just downright terrifying things in the game. I wasn’t sure about the first person view at first but it ended up being a pretty good choice that the devs went with for this game.The sound design of the game was done incredibly well. I don’t have the best speaker setup but man, I could hear every little thing going on in the house which did not help my paranoia one bit lol. Not only that but the game ran pretty flawlessly on my 1440p ultrawide monitor so I didn’t have to fight against low framerate or stutters.

Then, there are the characters I mentioned before; so Resident Evil has always been character focused which is why I continue to enjoy this series despite the campiness and bad writing sometimes but the Baker family are something else. I don’t know who they got to do the acting but every single person in the family was stellar at making me feel like each one was dangerous in their own way. Jack in particular made me feel like that one scene from the Shining movie when I had no weapon or tools to fight him. Lucas gave me Saws vibe, and Marguerit…

This was a great addition to the Resident Evil series and a great return to the horror aspect of the game, I can't believe that I passed this game up for the longest time in favor of characters that i'm familiar with, within the RE series but Ethan was a decent character, not too much depth to him, i definitely like characters like Chris Redfield and Leon Kennedy more but it's also good that they are introducing more new characters  into the series, I think that's what makes the horror element to these games work much better also because not everyone in these games is some battle hardened, experienced veteran of fighting these monsters, and the jumpscares worked better in this than many other games, so i'm glad they returned to a more story-driven horror game, and this game runs really good on the PC, i didn't have any issues running the game in the first place, so that was a really nice bonus also, i didn't have to go through hoops to get the game running, it was a simple install and run with great detail to the graphics and a solid story and good progression and it's not overly long too, so overall, great addition, definitely recommend for everyone to  play if you enjoy the resident evil series

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as having unskippable cutscenes that negatively impact replayability.

citations.review_text:
Capcom took a franchise that was bleeding out through a wound of its own making (RE6 was a disaster, RE5 was a colonial mess) and pivoted it into first-person survival horror with the confidence of someone who knows the original recipe still works. RE7 is a reset button that actually respects the fanbase instead of ignoring them.

The shift to first-person is the whole game — it makes ammo scarcity feel claustrophobic, puzzle-solving intimate, and the Baker family actually terrifying because you're at their eye level in their dingy mansion instead of orchestrating some third-person power fantasy. That change alone rebuilds the tension that the franchise abandoned around 2009. The atmosphere is oppressive (swamps, decay, isolation), the horror is grungy and grotesque rather than action-movie spectacle, and Ethan Winters' voicelessness (he doesn't speak) leaves room for you to be the protagonist instead of watching some dude react.

The story beats are solid Southern Gothic horror — deranged family, body horror, psychological breakdown — wrapped in the RE formula without feeling like cosplay. VR support exists and allegedly makes it genuinely unhinged, but standard first-person is plenty immersive on its own.

Boss design can be frustrating (some difficulty spikes feel arbitrary, unskippable cutscenes on repeat deaths are tedious), and 40%+ of players quit before finishing, which suggests it's not for everyone. But 95% of over 100,000 Steam reviews are positive, with Metacritic scoring it 86. It's the franchise's return to honest survival horror instead of tentpole spectacle.

Get it on sale for $8. It's worth reclaiming a franchise from the brink.

honestly, its good the first time.  and maybe the second time.  but not the third consecutive playthrough, or the fourth, or the fifth.  too many unskippable cutscenes.  They keep giving this guy games to make tedious i cant stand it.
Always a great game to replay but the unskippable cutscenes sour the taste a bit

A strong atmosphere, a solid survival horror experience and the Baker family make this game iconic. Definitely hits different compared to other RE games, but it's a solid entry still.

A couple nitpicks:
- Item collection isn't as satisfying as in the other modern RE games (as in the map doesn't go blue).
- Enemies sometimes pull of an insta-bite, dealing an insane amount of damage that feels unfair.
- The Magnum is not worth the effort of obtaining it (it costs a lot and a shotgun is just as good).
- Almost every cutscene being unskippable doesn't do any favors for the game's replay-ability.

DLC overview:
- "Not a Hero" adds an extra Chris Redfield campaign. You can parry attacks in this one, which is alright. Also comes with a "Professional" difficulty that makes sure you learn to parry. Not part of the Season pass, but free.
- "End of Zoe" adds an extra first-person beat-em-up campaign that's just pure fun.
- "Banned Footage Vol.1" adds a wave-defense mode (meh), an escape room (not much to see) and "Ethan Must Die" (tough).
- "Banned Footage Vol.2" adds black jack (twisted, but alright), more story (pretty good) and an arcade style collectathon (silly, but ok).
- The coin DLCs aren't worth it (and not necessary for achievements).
[hr][/hr]
100% achievement completion boils down finding all collectibles, completing challenge runs and beating all high-difficulty modes the game and its DLCs have to offer. This will take multiple playthroughs. There's plenty of detailed guides and walkthroughs out there, which help with everything. Overall, the difficulty can be frustrating (especially in the Ethan Must Die DLC), but it's manageable.

Item variety: Standard
Guns: Just like the classic RE games
Puzzles: Entertaining and creative

A return to the horrific Resident Evil formula putting the player in a isolated location where they are hunted by disturbing creatures and have to solve puzzles in order to escape. Ethan is a blank slate and in this game I have no issue with it as Capcom wanted a fresh start putting the player as more of the focus than the character due to the first person view. This is also the first RE to introduce the RE (reach for the moon) engine that brought great graphics alongside performance. the story of this game is very interesting on a first playthrough giving us intrigue on the why the Bakers are the way they are. But I feel the molded are very repetitive enemies with little variety also the games great pacing comes to a complete halt at the 80% mark  I also dislike the character of Mia Winters who is given too much sympathy for being a child trafficking bio terrorist. This is a good return to Residents evil roots but does faulter in some aspects that made the originals so phenominal. 6/10
Glad they stepped away from the formula that made six. Horror element was amazing but the enemies were lacking in variety. 8/10

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the later portion of the game, specifically the ship section, drags or becomes less enjoyable compared to the opening hours.

citations.review_text:
Resident Evil Biohazard is a pure masterpiece. The game took my breath away. The story is so magnificent, and the game looks great considering it was published in 2017. The story about the Baker family is amazing and moving. There were a few bits where I got bored (the boat), but that's just because of my goldfish attention span. Otherwise, it's amazing. I enjoyed every scene of this game, and if I could play this game again for the first time, I gladly would.

It's scary, and the jump scares get you good, but there are so many moments where it's just atmospherically scary and keeps you on your toes. I cannot recommend this game enough for someone who wants a good horror game.

5/5

Felt like doing a replay after 6 years because of the vibes and atmosphere that I remember enjoying, but the game design is just complete ass, far worse than I remember. Terrible damage sponge bosses, stalkers that will randomly just know exactly where you are with no audio or visual indication and beeline for you, enemies that somehow lunge at you in a straight line around corners, getting a game over from watching a VHS tape (and no, it's not The Ring), 100% scripted enemy appearances so there's no tension whatsoever while exploring. Overall the game is just really subpar aside from the visual design. I remember the ship section absolutely sucking too so I did myself a favor by dropping it before getting to that part.

RE series has a few of my favorite games of all time, but this sure ain't one of them. Definitely won't ever be replaying this one again.
i thought that this would be the scariest RE game but it was the most fun until the ship part but overall it's a great game
would be the best re game including the amazing dlcs but the second half of this game is just a pain in the ass to play

9/10 Definitely worth the play if you like gritty and grotesque Horror games
 
Scary as hell. Even during my second playthrough the sounds, jump scares and overall gameplay kept catching me off guard and kept me on my toes - especially the basement. The only thing I would say is that when you get to the end of the game [shipwreck] things do start to drag and can oftentimes be confusing on the map layout.
